text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.
* Italian authorities focused on speed as a possible cause for the derailment of a Milan-to-Rome express in northern Italy that killed eight people on Sunday (all).

* Centre-right deputies are due to meet today to endorse a unified position on the set-up of a bicameral commission to carry out constitutional reforms. Freedom Alliance leader Silvio Berlusconi, who backs the proposal and has negotiated closely with leftist Pds leader Massimo D'Alema, will try to avoid a row with hard-right leader Gianfranco Fini (all).

* Italian shares continued their rally buoyed by strong domestic buying interest, higher bonds and a firmer lira. The all-share Mibtel index rose 2.26 percent on Monday, while bond futures and the lira closed at record highs.

* Bank of Italy governor Antonio Fazio said average 1997 CPI should fall below three percent but added "risks for inflation come from public finance and labour costs and monetary policy has to reflect these things" cooling hopes of an imminent discount rate cut (all).
* Engineering employers association Federmeccanica might come up with a new proposal on the metalworkers contract renewal after an extraordinary general meeting today (all).

* A deal between information technology group Olivetti and a consortium of investors over the sale of Olivetti's ailing pc division is expected to be announced in the coming days. The consortium is led by US financier Edward Gottesman and Gianmario Rossignolo, chiarman of Electrolux unit Zanussi (La Stampa, Corriere).

* In an interview, undersecretary to the Industry minister Filippo Cavazzuti says phone operator Telecom and its parent Stet, which the government plans to merge, should "concentrate on fixed-line and mobile telephony and sell all other industrial activieties which are not core business for the new group" (Sole 24 Ore).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
